drhp.business: Alpine Texworld manufactures Grey Fabric and Yarn and provides yarn-sizing job work, operating a weaving unit (112 Toyota air-jet looms) and a spinning unit (open-end rotor) in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, plus a 72-loom weaving unit through its subsidiary Alpine Cottweave LLP. It sells predominantly to fabric processors/traders in Gujarat, and has pursued backward integration into yarn to reduce reliance on third-party yarn purchases.
drhp.end_markets: Domestic textile processors/traders, predominantly Gujarat (~97% of revenue); minor sales to Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Haryana
drhp.expansion: Setting up Proposed Manufacturing Unit 3 (48 additional looms, +77.50 lakh metres/annum grey fabric, ~28% capacity increase) on company-owned land at Survey No. 1098 adjacent to existing units, targeted for commercial production by March 2027 and funded from the fresh issue. Separately, an additional spinning-and-weaving unit is planned to be funded via debt and internal accruals.

internal_operational.detail: A material portion of consolidated revenue and PAT is contributed by the subsidiary; any underperformance, loss of customers or operational disruption at the subsidiary would adversely affect consolidated results.
internal_operational.evidence: For Fiscal 2026 Alpine Cottweave LLP contributed ₹ 1,229.98 million (35.89% of consolidated revenue from operations) and ₹ 83.78 million to consolidated PAT excluding NCI (38.58% of total).

internal_operational.detail: Order placed for 48 airjet looms from Picanol NV under a letter of credit; other capex orders (domestic machinery, building, electrification) not yet placed and are subject to quotation expiry, cost escalation, technology lock-in and forex exposure on imported spares.

internal_operational.title: Imported machinery procurement and cost-overrun risk for Proposed Unit 3

internal_operational.title: Leasehold dependence including from related party

strategy_growth.detail: Promoters will hold a majority of outstanding Equity Shares post-Issue and can control the Board and shareholder decisions, potentially conflicting with minority interests.
strategy_growth.evidence: Promoters to hold majority of outstanding Equity Shares after the Issue.
strategy_growth.title: Continued control by Promoters after the Issue

strategy_growth.detail: Majority of revenue comes from one segment, exposing the Company to demand reduction, competition, technology change and raw-material price/availability risk.
strategy_growth.evidence: Grey Fabric revenue ₹ 3,313.85 million, ₹ 2,139.97 million and ₹ 1,728.58 million = 96.69%, 90.17% and 94.15% for Fiscal 2026/2025/2024.
strategy_growth.title: Revenue concentration in a single business segment (Grey Fabric)

strategy_growth.detail: Manufacturing and sales are concentrated in Gujarat, making operations susceptible to regional social, environmental and economic disruptions.
strategy_growth.evidence: Gujarat revenue ₹ 3,336.85 million, ₹ 2,310.04 million and ₹ 1,791.36 million = 97.37%, 97.34% and 97.57% of revenue from operations for Fiscal 2026/2025/2024.
strategy_growth.title: Geographic concentration in Gujarat

strategy_growth.detail: Past growth is not indicative of future results; the Company may be unable to sustain historical growth rates or execute strategies amid changing market dynamics and competition.
strategy_growth.title: Historical growth may not be sustainable

strategy_growth.detail: Promoter Directors hold a large majority of pre-Issue capital and are interested beyond remuneration, retaining significant control over Board composition and shareholder votes.

strategy_growth.detail: Most directors lack experience as directors of a public listed company, which entails heightened compliance, governance and reporting demands.
strategy_growth.evidence: Only Sumit Champalal Agarwal and Piyush Ravishanker Bhatt have public listed-company directorship experience.
strategy_growth.title: Limited listed-company experience among Directors

concerns_observed: Corporate guarantee of Rs 5,575 lakh (Rs 557.50 million) extended by the Company and Promoter Group company Alpine Weaving Pvt Ltd to secure subsidiary Alpine Cottweave LLP's Saraswat consortium facilities equals 76.49% of FY26 consolidated net worth of Rs 7,288.4 lakh; it may crystallise on any subsidiary default.

CRISIL downgraded the long-term rating from 'CRISIL BBB-/Stable' to 'CRISIL BB/Stable' and short-term from 'A3' to 'A4+' with an 'Issuer Not Cooperating' remark on June 15, 2026, following a fee dispute and the Company's request to withdraw CRISIL services.

Heavy dependence on government subsidies for reported profit: total subsidy (net SGST refund, electricity duty, interest subsidy) of Rs 1,096.8 / 359.7 / 502.3 lakh equalled 50.50% / 41.70% / 102.91% of PAT for FY26 / FY25 / FY24.
High leverage: total debt Rs 17,776.1 lakh against net worth Rs 7,288.4 lakh (D/E ~2.4x) with cash of only Rs 130.1 lakh at FY26; secured debt is floating-rate.

Customer concentration: top 10 customers were 71.86% / 70.19% / 70.33% of revenue and the single largest 13.64% / 8.77% / 16.09% (FY24/25/26), with no long-term commitments and correlated cluster credit risk.
Supplier concentration: top 10 suppliers were 81.43% / 82.76% / 64.26% of purchases and the top supplier up to 25.58%, without long-term supply contracts.

Related-party land acquisitions from Promoter/Director Sumit Champalal Agarwal and Promoter Group member Champalal Gopiram Agarwal aggregating Rs 786.4 lakh (Gangad Rs 360 lakh plus three Aslali parcels of Rs 29.3 / 155.3 / 241.8 lakh), each acquired below stated market value.
Concentrated single-product, single-state profile: Grey Fabric was 96.69% of FY26 revenue and Gujarat 97.37%; 100% domestic, leaving negligible product or geographic diversification.
Subsidiary dependence: Alpine Cottweave LLP contributed 35.89% of FY26 consolidated revenue and 38.58% of PAT (ex-NCI), concentrating consolidated results in one recently acquired entity.
Very high workforce churn: employee attrition 26.39% / 14.46% / 76.92% and KMP/SMP attrition 50.00% / 0.00% / 18.18% across FY24/25/26.
Unsecured related-party and other loans of Rs 3,243.7 lakh (consolidated, at 9-12% p.a.) are repayable on demand, a recall risk to liquidity.

Manufacturing Unit 2 commenced operations on March 28, 2025 before obtaining the GPCB Consolidated Consent and Authorization; the Company paid Rs 19.8 lakh regularisation and received CCA only on January 16, 2026.

Bonus issue of 7:1 (Dec 21, 2020) and two name changes in the run-up to filing (last on Feb 10, 2025); promoter average acquisition cost of Rs 1.99 / 2.52 / 8.01 per share is far below the intended issue price.
data_gaps: Operating cash flow (CFO) not disclosed in the extracted domains for any of FY24-FY26; only CFI and CFF are available.
Balance-sheet detail missing: net fixed assets, CWIP, inventory, trade receivables and trade payables are null across all three years, and total debt is disclosed only for FY26.
P&L line items other_income, depreciation and finance cost are largely null (finance cost given only for FY24 at 850.1 lakh).
Employee strength (headcount) not disclosed in the provided DRHP text.
Post-issue promoter holding, dilution percentage, pledge percentage and final issue price band are not disclosed (price band TBD).
Receivables ageing (amount over 1 year) not quantified as of March 31, 2026.
Subsidiary Alpine Cottweave LLP and Group Company standalone audited financials are not reproduced in the DRHP (stated to be available on the website).
monitorables: Subsidiary Alpine Cottweave LLP performance (35.89% of consolidated revenue, 38.58% of PAT ex-NCI in FY26) and any movement toward invocation of the Rs 5,575 lakh guarantee.
Trajectory of government subsidies as a share of PAT and any policy change, delay or claw-back under the Gujarat Textile Policy 2012.
Credit-rating actions - whether CRISIL cooperation resumes/improves and whether CARE's BBB-/A3 holds, given floating-rate secured debt.
Leverage and liquidity: post-IPO debt reduction (Rs 5,220 lakh objects), the Rs 3,243.7 lakh on-demand unsecured loans, and cash of only Rs 130.1 lakh against Rs 17,776.1 lakh total debt.
Execution of Proposed Unit 3 (Rs 3,071.1 lakh) - placement of the outstanding 10.46% machinery plus building/electrification orders, cost overruns and the Mar 2027 commissioning target.
Customer and supplier concentration ratios and any conversion to firm/long-term contracts.
Employee and KMP attrition trends after the FY26 spike (76.92% employee, 18.18% KMP).
Resolution of pending compliance items: WTCS compounding application, RoC filing discrepancies, GPCB CCA renewals, and trademark registration under classes 23/24/35.
open_questions: What is the standalone financial health of subsidiary Alpine Cottweave LLP (its own leverage, liquidity and covenant status) that underlies the Rs 5,575 lakh corporate guarantee, and what events would trigger invocation?
What was consolidated operating cash flow (CFO) for FY24-FY26, given only CFI and CFF are disclosed and reported PAT is subsidy-dependent?

What core profitability remains after excluding government subsidies, which were 50.50% of FY26 PAT and exceeded 100% of FY24 PAT, and how durable are the Gujarat Textile Policy SGST/electricity/interest subsidies?
What drove the CRISIL 'Issuer Not Cooperating' downgrade beyond the stated surveillance-fee dispute, and why do CRISIL (BB) and CARE (BBB-) diverge by two notches?

Were the related-party land parcels (Rs 786.4 lakh) and the below-market leases from Alpine Weaving Pvt Ltd independently valued, and how were arm's-length terms established given each was below stated market value?
What explains the 76.92% employee attrition and 18.18% KMP/SMP attrition in FY26, and its impact on plant operations?
What are the repayment triggers and lender relationships behind the Rs 3,243.7 lakh unsecured loans repayable on demand?
How will the Company mitigate customer credit risk given ~70% of revenue sits with the top 10 customers in one Gujarat textile cluster with no long-term contracts?

parameter_scores.basis: Consolidated revenue 18,360.3 -> 23,732.4 -> 34,271.3 lakh (FY24-26), ~37% two-year CAGR; PAT 488.1 -> 862.6 -> 2,171.6 lakh.
EBITDA margin rose 10.84% -> 13.84% and PAT margin 2.66% -> 6.34% (FY24-26), but 50.50% of FY26 PAT and 102.91% of FY24 PAT came from government subsidies, so core margin is materially thinner.
Subsidies were 50.50% / 41.70% / 102.91% of PAT (FY26/25/24); operating cash flow not disclosed in the extracted domains; profit leans on schemes that can be reduced, delayed or clawed back.
Total debt 17,776.1 lakh vs net worth 7,288.4 lakh (D/E ~2.4x), cash only 130.1 lakh at FY26, plus 3,243.7 lakh unsecured loans repayable on demand.
Rs 5,575 lakh corporate guarantee for subsidiary Alpine Cottweave LLP equals 76.49% of FY26 net worth; sole disclosed contingent item and material relative to equity.

CRISIL BB/Stable and A4+ with 'Issuer Not Cooperating' (downgraded from BBB-/A3 on June 15, 2026 amid a fee dispute); CARE separately rates BBB-/A3 (May 4, 2026) - a two-notch split and a cooperation flag.
Negative CFI of (3,237.0) / (9,450.3) / (806.4) lakh and CFF of (308.7) / 8,234.6 / (2,278.3) lakh across FY26/25/24; operating cash flow not disclosed in the extracted domains.
Top 10 customers 71.86% / 70.19% / 70.33% of revenue; top customer up to 16.09%; no firm/long-term commitments and correlated Gujarat-cluster credit risk.
Top 10 suppliers 81.43% / 82.76% / 64.26% of purchases; top supplier up to 25.58%; no long-term supply contracts amid cotton-price/seasonality volatility.
Grey Fabric 96.69% of FY26 revenue and Gujarat 97.37%; 100% domestic; single-product, single-state exposure.

Related-party land purchases (Rs 786.4 lakh) below market value, below-market leases from Promoter Group Alpine Weaving (MU2 rent 0.60m vs market 1.80m), 3,243.7 lakh related/other unsecured loans, and past SEBI penalties on Promoter Group member Champalal Gopiram Agarwal (Rs 5 lakh, 5 lakh and 100 lakh orders in 2018).

Unit 2 operated pre-GPCB CCA (Rs 19.8 lakh regularisation); delayed WTCS appointment (compounding pending); RoC filing discrepancies/untraceable forms; trademark only 'Marked for Exam'; MSME payments beyond the 45-day limit.

Promoter pre-issue holding 90.36% with personal guarantees on Company borrowings, but average acquisition cost of Rs 1.99 / 2.52 / 8.01 per share for the three promoters is far below the intended issue price and a 7:1 bonus was issued in Dec 2020.

Objects split Rs 3,071.1 lakh Unit 3 capex, Rs 5,220 lakh debt repayment, GCP <=25%; but objects not appraised by any bank/FI, 10.46% of Unit 3 machinery plus building and electrification orders not yet placed, commercial production targeted only Mar 2027.

red_flags: Rs 5,575 lakh corporate guarantee for subsidiary Alpine Cottweave LLP equal to 76.49% of FY26 consolidated net worth (Rs 7,288.4 lakh) - an off-balance-sheet exposure that could crystallise on subsidiary default.
CRISIL downgrade to BB/Stable and A4+ with 'Issuer Not Cooperating' (June 15, 2026) following a fee dispute, while CARE separately rates BBB-/A3 - a two-notch split and a cooperation red flag.
Reported profit is subsidy-dependent: government subsidies were 50.50% / 41.70% / 102.91% of PAT for FY26/25/24, implying FY24 was loss-making before subsidies.

Related-party land acquisitions (Rs 786.4 lakh) below stated market value and below-market leases from Promoter/Promoter Group entities, alongside prior SEBI penalties on Promoter Group member Champalal Gopiram Agarwal.
Manufacturing Unit 2 ran before obtaining GPCB Consolidated Consent and Authorization, requiring a Rs 19.8 lakh regularisation - a compliance gap the DRHP flags could recur at Proposed Unit 3.
strengths_observed: Rapid top-line growth: consolidated revenue rose from Rs 18,360.3 lakh (FY24) to Rs 23,732.4 lakh (FY25) to Rs 34,271.3 lakh (FY26), roughly 37% two-year CAGR.
Margin expansion alongside scale: EBITDA margin improved from 10.84% (FY24) to 11.38% (FY25) to 13.84% (FY26); PAT margin from 2.66% to 6.34% over the same period.
Strong headline return ratios for FY26: ROE 33.85%, RONW 29.44%, ROCE 17.56%, up from ROE 12.17% / ROCE 12.12% in FY24.
High capacity utilisation of the weaving base: 95.41% (FY24), 106.51% (FY25) and 107.30% (FY26) on installed 276 lakh metres, indicating demand absorption of existing assets.

Backward integration executed: in-house spinning (Manufacturing Unit 2, commissioned Mar 2025, 88.5% utilisation FY26) plus acquisition of 97% of weaving subsidiary Alpine Cottweave LLP, reducing reliance on third-party yarn.
Captive solar lowered power intensity: power and fuel expense fell from 5.53% of revenue (FY24) to 4.30% (FY26) with 820 KW + 475 KW rooftop and 5.4 MW + 3.6 MW ground-mounted solar installed.
Deleveraging intent in the objects: Rs 5,220 lakh of fresh-issue proceeds earmarked to prepay/repay Saraswat and SVC bank cash-credit and term-loan facilities.

Largest single machinery order already placed: 48 Picanol NV air-jet looms (Rs 2,115.3 lakh, 89.54% of Unit 3 plant-and-machinery capex) contracted under LC, reducing part of the execution risk on the expansion.
